widgetMetadata.instructions: Each entry under `widgets` describes one chart/widget rendered on this page of the Israeli Ecosystem dashboard. Descriptions are result-agnostic: they explain what the visualization shows and how to interpret it, not the specific numbers. The `dataPaths` array on each entry lists dot-notation paths inside this same JSON file where the underlying data for that widget lives (e.g. "kpis.patentingStartups" or "ipIntensity.items") When summarizing or answering questions about a number from this snapshot, locate the relevant widget(s) by `dataPaths` and quote the corresponding `description` to explain the metric. Widgets that have a 10 year trend usually show the total overall (across all years) and you get the exact data for each year in the past 10 years. The 10 year data do not add up to the total of course

startups:map.title: Israel Startup Map
startups:map.description: Geographic distribution of Israeli startups by their registered address in Israel. Each city marker is sized by the number of startups with an active legal registration in that city and colored by its administrative district. The legend lists the same totals by district. Only startups with a known registered Israeli address appear.

startups:kpi-total-startups.title: Total Startups
startups:kpi-total-startups.description: Total number of Israeli startups in the dataset (active, exited, and closed combined). The bar chart shows new startups by founding year over the past 10 years.

startups:kpi-funding-rounds.title: Funding Rounds
startups:kpi-funding-rounds.description: Total number of equity rounds raised by Israeli startups across all time: money paid into the company for newly issued shares, from pre-seed through late stage, including SAFEs, convertible notes and bridges. The bar chart shows the count of rounds closed each year over the past 10 years.

startups:kpi-total-raised.title: Total Raised
startups:kpi-total-raised.description: Total capital (USD) Israeli startups raised in equity rounds: money paid into the company for newly issued shares, from pre-seed through late stage, including SAFEs, convertible notes and bridges. The bar chart shows the dollar amount raised each year over the past 10 years.

startups:kpi-acquisitions.title: Acquisitions
startups:kpi-acquisitions.description: Total number of Israeli startups that exited via a completed acquisition, meaning a deal that actually went ahead. The bar chart shows acquisitions by exit year over the past 10 years.

startups:kpi-ipos.title: IPOs
startups:kpi-ipos.description: Total number of Israeli startups that exited via IPO and reached the market, meaning shares priced or trading on a public exchange. The bar chart shows IPOs by exit year over the past 10 years.

startups:kpi-time-to-exit.title: Time to Exit
startups:kpi-time-to-exit.description: Average number of years between founding year and exit year (acquisition or IPO) across all exited Israeli startups. The histogram shows the distribution of those exit times in 1-year buckets, capped at 30+ years.

startups:survival-distribution.title: Survival Distribution
startups:survival-distribution.description: Breakdown of all Israeli startups by current status: Active (still operating), Closed (shut down or dissolved), and Exit (acquired or went public). The center of the donut shows the total number of startups, or the value of the hovered slice.

startups:exit-funnel.title: Exit Funnel
startups:exit-funnel.description: How many Israeli startups make it through each progressive milestone toward an exit: All startups (everyone in the dataset), Funded (raised at least one equity round), $1M+ (raised at least $1 million in total), $10M+ (raised at least $10 million in total), Exit (a completed acquisition or public listing). The percentage on each segment is the retention from the All-startups stage.

startups:time-to-exit.title: Time To Exit
startups:time-to-exit.description: Average and median number of years between founding year and exit year (acquisition or IPO) across all exited Israeli startups. The histogram below shows the distribution of those exit times in 1-year buckets, with the rightmost bucket capturing every exit at 30 or more years.

startups:industry-mix.title: Industry Share Over Time
startups:industry-mix.description: Stacked bar chart of the industry mix of Israeli startups by founding year. Each bar is one year, broken into 6 industry categories (IT and Telecom, Healthcare and Food, Consumer Goods and Services, Energy and Utilities, Financial Services, Media and Entertainment). Sub-industries that fall outside these 6 are bucketed into Unknown and excluded from the visible mix. The legend on the right shows each industry overall total and share across all years.

startups:signal-deeptech.title: Deeptech
startups:signal-deeptech.description: Share of Israeli startups flagged as deeptech. Deep tech companies require significant resources, long development cycles, specialized expertise, and substantial investment. The 10-segment meter visualizes that share. The number on the right is the absolute count of deeptech startups.

startups:signal-global.title: Operating Globally
startups:signal-global.description: Share of Israeli startups that have a product with a global audience. The 10-segment meter visualizes that share. The number on the right is the absolute count of globally operating startups.

startups:trending-up.title: Sub-Industries Trending Up By Share Of Total
startups:trending-up.description: Top 5 sub-industries whose share of new Israeli startups has grown the most over the past 10 founding years. Each line is one sub-industry. The value at year Y is the share of startups founded in year Y whose primary sub-industry falls in that group. The dashed tail marks the most recent year, which is still incomplete.

startups:trending-down.title: Sub-Industries Trending Down By Share Of Total
startups:trending-down.description: Top 5 sub-industries whose share of new Israeli startups has shrunk the most over the past 10 founding years. Each line is one sub-industry. The value at year Y is the share of startups founded in year Y whose primary sub-industry falls in that group. The dashed tail marks the most recent year, which is still incomplete.

startups:feed-funding.title: Funding Feed
startups:feed-funding.description: Latest funding rounds added to the dataset, gathered from multiple verifiable sources. Unlike the headline funding figures, this feed carries every round type, grants and venture debt included, each one flagged with isNonEquity so you can tell them apart.

startups:feed-new-startups.title: New Startups
startups:feed-new-startups.description: Latest startups added to the dataset. Not necessarily new Startups founded.

startups:feed-notable.title: Notable Events
startups:feed-notable.description: Latest notable events gathered form news feeds, including acquisitions, IPOs, corporate events, strategic partnerships and more.

notable.summary: CX2 launched Vadris SDR, a software-defined radio version of its Vadris RF direction-finding payload, expanding detection across FPV control protocols (ExpressLRS, TBS Crossfire, DJI OcuSync). More than 450 Vadris systems have been fielded to the U.S. Department of War.

Acquired by Nebius (Nasdaq: NBIS). Nebius announced it acquired Inferize, with the team and technology joining Nebius Token Factory, its managed inference platform. Terms were officially undisclosed; press reports estimated $100-150 million (Calcalist) / $100-130 million (Globes). Inferize, founded January 2026 by Guy Bortnikov and Lior Gorbonos (Granulate alums) with 17 Tel Aviv employees and a Seed round led by TLV Partners, was sold before commercial launch.

Surpassed $1 billion in cumulative total transaction value (TTV) processed through its platform; company connects tens of thousands of hotels with thousands of travel companies and technology providers.

Rig Security emerged from stealth, launching its AI-native identity protection platform that correlates human, machine and AI identities (RICE correlation engine and Bifrost endpoint sensor) across cloud, on-premises, identity-provider and endpoint environments, providing ISPM and ITDR including runtime policy enforcement over AI agents. Already in production with Fortune 200 organizations and available on AWS and CrowdStrike Marketplaces.

Acquired by Valley National Bancorp (parent of Valley National Bank) for approximately $340 million (~75% cash / 25% Valley common stock, ~$255M cash plus ~6.3M shares). Definitive agreement announced September 28, 2026; expected to close early 2027 subject to regulatory approvals. Bluevine brings ~$2.1 billion of deposits and ~175,000 active small-business customers; co-founder and CEO Eyal Lifshitz is expected to join Valley as Head of Small Business Banking after closing. Cantor Fitzgerald and Wachtell Lipton advised Valley; Financial Technology Partners and Sidley Austin advised Bluevine.

Announced definitive agreement for a SPAC merger with Bold Eagle Acquisition Corp (Nasdaq: BEAG) at a $1.25 billion pre-money enterprise valuation, with $335 million of committed capital anchored by Loomis, Sayles & Co. including investment from AE Industrial and Eagle Equity Partners; Paragon (already owned by AE Industrial and merged into portfolio company REDLattice) will constitute the lion's share of the combined entity, which reported combined revenue of $267 million and 750 employees.

Cotton Queen, a Sudanese feature film co-produced by Storming Donkey Productions alongside Strange Bird GmbH, Jip Film und Verleih, Maneki Films and others, continued its international festival run with screenings in Doha (September 23-27, in collaboration with the Doha Film Institute). The film premiered in Critics' Week competition at the 82nd Venice International Film Festival and won awards including the FIFHD Grand Prize, the Doha Film Festival Audience Award and the Thessaloniki Golden Alexander 'Theo Angelopoulos' Award for Best Feature Film.
Received the 2026 IoT Evolution Product of the Year Award for the second consecutive year, for its Software-Defined Connectivity Cloud.

Island was recognized by industry analysts: Frost & Sullivan named it the 2026 Global Zero Trust Browser Security Company of the Year, and Island was named a Customers' Choice in the 2026 Gartner Peer Insights Voice of the Customer for Secure Enterprise Browsers (announced in the company's Series F press release).

Acquired Wand Cloud, an Israeli startup whose technology automatically optimizes Kubernetes, for a reported tens of millions of dollars — groundcover's first acquisition, combining its production visibility with Wand's optimization technology.

Acquired by FIMI Opportunity Funds: the Israeli private equity firm acquired 55% control of MMDSmart for $55 million, with most proceeds flowing into the company for growth. Founders Arie Frenklakh and Leonid Rubanov retain 45% and continue leading the company (annual revenue ~NIS 500 million).

Acquired by groundcover for several tens of millions of dollars (terms undisclosed). groundcover's first acquisition; Wand's founding team (Shon Lev-Ran, Shir Monether) and 10 employees join groundcover to combine Kubernetes resource optimization with groundcover's observability platform.
WEIR AI introduced the ʳᵖ mark, a public symbol signaling that a person's identity is protected and licensable, analogous to © and ™.

Acquired Aegis, an Israeli AI security startup founded in early 2026 by Unit 8200 veterans Omri Limor and Saar Ankonina, in a stock transaction reportedly valued around $30M (terms not officially disclosed). The Aegis co-founders join Upwind to lead the newly established Upwind AI Security Labs, focused on detecting and defending against threats involving AI agents, tools and plugins; the labs team is planned to grow from 12 to ~25-35 researchers.

Following the sale of its defense business to Ondas, Paul Kandel (previously VP Business Development) was promoted to Managing Director with responsibility for Ottopia's strategy, operations and commercial growth; Alex Kirshon continues as Chief Technology Officer, and founder Amit Rosenzweig departs to lead Ottopia Defense within Ondas.

Acquired by Ondas Inc. — Ondas acquired Ottopia's defense business (completed September 23, 2026; transaction dated August 31, 2026), as part of a three-business deal with Insignito Ltd. and CaribouLabs Ltd. for aggregate consideration of approximately $60.38 million paid in Ondas stock (7,821,445 shares), plus a potential aggregate earnout of up to $32 million tied to performance milestones through 2028. Ottopia founder/CEO Amit Rosenzweig joins Ondas to lead Ottopia Defense, while Ottopia's remaining commercial business refocuses on software for deploying, supervising and scaling autonomous vehicles and robotic systems (Physical AI).
Terminated the securities purchase agreement with the Rain Foundation under which it had agreed, subject to shareholder approval, to sell and issue ordinary shares to the Rain Foundation.
Expanded its European critical infrastructure security capabilities through its HySecurity division.
Ivalua was named a Leader in the IDC MarketScape: Worldwide AI-Enabled Direct Spend evaluation.

Acquired by Cognex Corporation: Cognex (NASDAQ: CGNX) signed a definitive agreement to acquire RealSense for approximately $500 million in cash (total deal value ~$600 million including a $56.5M retention program and ~$50M in RSUs), expanding into robotic perception and Physical AI. Expected to close in Q4 2026; prior to closing, RealSense will spin out its Facial Authentication product line into an independent biometrics company. RealSense expects $80-90M revenue in 2026 (50%+ growth).
